The dumper addon now handles `HttpConnectErrorHook`, so failed CONNECT requests (for example DNS resolution errors) are printed in mitmdump. I haven't run the tests, as you asked.

- **`mitmproxy/addons/dumper.py`:** I added `http_connect_error(self, f)`. It calls `echo_flow(f)` if the flow matches the view filter, the same way `error` does. `echo_flow` already prints the request line, and it prints the error message when `flow.error` is set. The hook's docstring says `flow.error` isn't guaranteed to be set here, in which case only the request line prints.
- **`CHANGELOG.md`:** I added an entry under "Unreleased".
- **`test/mitmproxy/addons/test_dumper.py`:** I added `test_http_connect_error`. It builds a CONNECT flow with an error, calls the hook, and checks that "CONNECT" and "error" appear in the output.

The `dumper.py` change and the changelog entry were already in the working tree when I looked, although the git status at the start of the session showed neither file modified. I kept them and added only the test.
